headline: Ward 27's growth explains its building lead and its worst-in-city raw counts alike.
summary:
Ward 27 leads Chicago on every measure of new building. It posted the most reported construction investment in new residential permits of any ward, at $279.7 million, and the largest estimate of new housing units on the way, at 633, with the most permits issued too. Two small businesses opened on West Town's Chicago Avenue this summer alone, a crowdfunded Basque pintxos bar and Joe Freshgoods's new store and cafe, real evidence of the same building wave the permit data describes. Arts and culture space nearly matches that lead, with 13 mapped venues, the second-most in the city. None of those numbers are a runaway victory. The gap between wards on the construction measures is narrow, only four or five points across the entire middle half of the city, so the ward's string of firsts is a slim margin over a crowded field of wards that are also building, not a wide lead over a slow city.

The weak rankings cluster in two different places, and both read differently once the ward's growth is the backdrop. The 607 traffic injuries and 173 pedestrian and cyclist crashes logged here both sit second-to-last in the city, but they come from the same crash log, and both are raw counts rather than rates. A ward adding this much new construction and this many new residents will log more incidents in absolute terms than a quieter one even at the same risk per person. The pollution numbers are a separate matter. Ward 27 ranks worst in the city for how close residents live to Superfund and brownfield sites, and near-worst for nearby toxic-release facilities, both pulled from the same environmental assessment. That pairing is one exposure profile read twice rather than two independent findings, and it is the part of this page the building boom does not explain.
reading_the_rankings: Two numbers here deserve more scrutiny than their rank suggests. The $256.4 million in TIF increment revenue is the flashiest of the ward's firsts, but it is also the softest, built by the same team that rates its own confidence in the figure low, and the comparison covers only 49 wards, one short of the full city. The pollution-proximity ranking needs a different kind of care. Worst in the city sounds like a precise reading for any one block, and the figure is spread across census tracts on the assumption that everyone inside a tract is affected evenly, so it describes the ward as a whole rather than a given address. The sites themselves do not move with the tract lines, and Ward 27 sits closer to more of them than any other ward in Chicago.

news.headline: Man Killed, Another Wounded By 5 Gunmen Outside River North Hotel
news.note: Five masked gunmen opened fire on two men outside a hotel in the 500 block of North State Street, killing a 30-year-old and wounding a 65-year-old.

news.headline: Gilda Basque Tavern Brings Spanish Pintxos To West Town With Crowdfunding Help
news.note: Three chef-partners raised $20,000 through crowdfunding to open a Basque-style pintxos bar on Chicago Avenue in West Town.

news.headline: Streetwear Icon Joe Freshgoods Is Back With Every Now And Then, A Store And Cafe In West Town
news.note: Designer Joe Freshgoods opened a permanent store and cafe, Josephine's, on West Chicago Avenue in West Town.

news.headline: Humboldt Park Neighbor Launches Fundraiser To Provide Swimsuits For Local Kids
news.note: A Humboldt Park resident started a GoFundMe for swimsuits after noticing kids at the pool going without proper swim gear because their families couldn't afford it.
